candidate.title: SCRB-Seq
candidate.scope: The middle row labeled SCRB-Seq in the assigned Illumina schematic: single-cell isolation, RNA preparation, per-cell oligonucleotide tagging/cDNA formation, pooling, broad post-pooling library preparation and PCR to cDNA. The row-left cell-to-highlighted-RNA drawing is a summary icon. The neighboring Div-Seq row and DNA Low-Level Detection/smMIP row are contextual, with no arrows or declared alternatives connecting them to the target row. Interpret the two misleading synthesis captions using the matched Soumillon et al. 2014 SCRB-Seq main-text architecture, without claiming a complete protocol, a specific optimization variant or identical chemistry for unshown adaptations.

method_scopes.rationale: The assigned card title, middle-row method label and literal Soumillon citation identify SCRB-Seq alone. All eight local operations belong to that row. The primary paper supports isolated-cell/well processing and barcoded, UMI-bearing cDNA formation before pooling; corrections c01 and c02 make that interpretation explicit while preserving the diagram route and captions. Applicability is resolved at the declared schematic scope. The exact division of the post-pooling library-preparation block is retained as a local nonblocking unknown, not assigned to another assay or variant.

corrections.primary_statement: The primary paper states that the pooled material is already decorated cDNA, and describes subsequent amplification and modified transposon-based preparation for multiplexed sequencing. Operation o07 therefore uses an already-cDNA substrate and a broad post-pooling library-preparation interpretation; it does not assert a second reverse-transcription reaction. The drawing’s route and following PCR remain intact. The main text does not establish a one-to-one mapping of the primary preparation steps onto this local caption.

checks.rationale: The supplied metadata establishes the paper identity, and its abstract reports transcriptional profiling in an inflammation study without naming SCRB-Seq or describing this library architecture. evidence.locator: PubMed metadata: title
evidence.quote: Cervicovaginal bacteria are a major modulator of host inflammatory responses in the female genital tract.

evidence.locator: Supplied abstract: transcriptional profiling passage
evidence.quote: Transcriptional profiling suggested that genital antigen-presenting cells sense gram-negative bacterial products in situ via Toll-like receptor 4 signaling, contributing to genital inflammation through activation of the NF-κB signaling pathway and recruitment of lymphocytes by chemokine production.

checks.rationale: The metadata identifies the reprogramming paper, while the supplied abstract names transcriptional and epigenomic analyses without establishing SCRB-Seq implementation or library preparation. Keeping methods=[] and the association unresolved is faithful to this abstract-only evidence. The reviewer accepts that limited assessment, not a positive or negative claim about SCRB-Seq use in unavailable full text.

evidence.quote: This system enabled integrative transcriptional and epigenomic analysis across the human reprogramming timeline at high resolution.

checks.rationale: The available main-text passage fixes cDNA formation and tagging before pooling and describes later amplification/transposon preparation, but does not map those reactions one-to-one onto the local post-Pool caption versus PCR. The candidate preserves that exact unresolved mapping, leaves s09 strand state and o07 chemistry broad, and identifies supplementary methods/figure evidence needed for a finer assignment. This is nonblocking at the declared schematic scope because target identity, carrier, tagging order, molecular pooling and all depicted transformations are represented without depending on that finer mapping.
